newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ consultant renamed Opus, sees 200 new hires.
newsitem.headline: NZ consultant renamed Opus, sees 200 new hires.

text.p: A Malaysian-owned consultancy group based in New Zealand said on Tuesday it planned to expand its environmental and technical skills base by hiring up to 200 new specialists in the coming 12 to 18 months.

In a statement Opus International Consultants, which has changed its name from Works Consultancy Services, said it planned to place recruitment ads in New Zealand and Britain to source the skills it needs for current and planned projects.

Opus chief executive John Rutledge said the new hires -- to include engineers, architects, designers and planners -- stemmed from an increasing workload and would build on an existing base of about 1,200 employees.
"I expect that we will be employing at least 1,500 people by the year 2000," he added.
Opus, formerly part of the New Zealand government's infrastructure management arm, was bought by Kinta Kellas, part of Malaysia's Renong group, for NZ$45.8 million last August.
It had chosen the new name because of its Latin meaning, "an accomplished work, a creation, an achievement", Rutledge said.
